Current telemetry shows sustained 120 QPS peak (internal API calls that average ~32 tokens/request). The product forecast is +3x peak QPS by end of Q1 and +2x by the time the renewal hits.

We need a proposal for:
- Updated reserved GPU pool to sustain 350–400 peak QPS with 95th percentile latency targets
- An option to burst above that for marketing spikes
- Any recommended changes to terms (term length, billing cadence) to lock pricing in while we ramp

I've attached the Q3 usage export for context. Who should I loop in from your side for sizing?

Subject: Arcadia — sizing input & ask ahead of client call (Thu 11am)

Team —

Quick prep before I hop on the 11am call with Arcadia on Thursday. Elaine shared an export (attached in upstream thread). High-level ask from them: support sustained 350–400 peak QPS with room to burst; target 95p latency SLA at their current model (65B family) and keep unit economics close to today.

Can you review and provide:
- Neha: a recommended GPU count and whether we should propose A100-80G equivalents vs. cheaper T4-style pool with scale-based routing
- Lauren: draft addendum language for committed pool sizing, burst credits, and a 12 vs 24 month term comparison (include short note on discount tiers for committed capacity)
- Connor: ops notes — autoscale safety margins, warm-cache sizing, and any caveats we should call out

Prelim sketch I ran:
- Current: 120 QPS peak * 32 tokens = ~3,840 tokens/sec => ~230k tokens/min
- Target peak (expected): 380 QPS * 32 tokens = ~12,160 tokens/sec => ~730k tokens/min
- Baseline GPU throughput (conservative): 90k tokens/min per A100-equivalent for this model family under our batched runtime
- Raw GPUs needed (no cache/batching optimizations): 730k / 90k ≈ 8.1 => round to 9 GPUs

That baseline ignores prefix caching, burst capacity, and scaling headroom. Neha — please sanity-check and produce two options (steady-state + burst pool) we can present. I'll summarize a pricing sketch once we have GPU counts.

Thanks — Sergio

Attachment: arcadia-usage-q3.csv (re-attached for team)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arcadia — sizing input & ask ahead of client call (Thu 11am)

Sergio / team —

I looked through the CSV and ran the sizing with conservative and optimized assumptions. Key assumptions first: average request = 32 tokens, 20% of traffic hits prefix-cached responses (saves ~40% of token work for those requests), and our batched runtime yields ~95k tokens/min per A100-eq when running mixed-length workloads with KV cache warm.

Option A — Conservative (no cache credit relied upon):
- Effective tokens/min target: 730k
- GPU throughput (A100-eq): 95k tokens/min
- GPUs required: 730k / 95k ≈ 7.7 → propose 8 GPUs reserved
- Recommended burst pool: +3 GPUs for marketing spikes (auto-burst to dedicated on short notice)
- Pros: simple SLA, lower risk; Cons: higher monthly commitment cost

Option B — Optimized (assume 20% cached & batching improvements):
- Effective tokens/min target after cache: 730k * 0.8 = 584k
- GPUs required: 584k / 95k ≈ 6.2 → propose 6 GPUs reserved
- Burst pool: +4 GPUs for spikes + a small auto-scale buffer
- Pros: lower baseline cost; Cons: requires cache warm strategy and conservative warm-up windows (we should model 2–5 minute warm windows)

Additional notes:
- Latency SLO (95p) — with 6–8 GPUs plus optimized routing and a 3-GPU burst buffer we can hit 95p targets for the current model family. Recommend specifying a burst SLA (minutes to spin up) in the addendum.
- Pricing guidance: pricing delta between 6 vs 8 GPUs is material (I estimate ~28% uplift for 8 vs 6 at current committed rates); include a monthly burst credit pool (hours) priced separately.

Recommendation for the customer-facing proposal: present both options — "Guaranteed 6 GPUs + 4 burst" (cost-efficient) and "Guaranteed 8 GPUs + 3 burst" (risk-reduced) with clear tradeoffs and a 12 vs 24 month discount table. I can help draft the technical appendix with the math.

-Neha
Senior Infra Engineer, Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference

Subject: Renewal proposal: Arcadia reserved pool options & next steps

Elaine / team —

Thanks again for the sync. Based on your forecast and Neha's sizing, please find below the two capacity + term options we recommend for the renewal. I've attached a proposed addendum (v2) that codifies committed GPUs, burst credits, and service levels.

Option 1 — Cost-efficient (recommended if you can rely on cache warm):
- Committed: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved
- Burst: 4 GPUs available on demand (pre-warmed pool + auto-burst)
- Expected 95p latency: meets target with 2–5 minute warm windows for rare cold prefixes
- Pricing: $XX,800 / month (12m) — see addendum; 24m term = 9% discounted rate

Option 2 — Risk-reduced (recommended if you want hard headroom):
- Committed: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved
- Burst: 3 GPUs available on demand
- Pricing: $XX,900 / month (12m) — 24m term = 11% discounted rate

Operational should-haves:
- Warm-cache plan: recommend a short scheduled cache-warm job during business hours for steady-state windows
- Burst SLA: 5-minute spin-up for the pre-warmed pool, documented in the addendum
- Quarterly review: throughput and token profile check to rebaseline pool sizing

Next steps:
1) Review the attached addendum (arcadia-proposed-addendum-v2.pdf) — I've highlighted the committed GPU counts and burst credit mechanics.
2) If acceptable, sign via the DocuSign link here: https://docusign.example/ARC-73-addendum 
3) We will schedule a runbook + warm-cache ops session with Connor and Jamal after the agreement is countersigned.

Would you like me to build a side-by-side TCO comparison (6 vs 8 GPUs) and present to your procurement team in the coming week?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
